title: A Three-Axis Stress Test of LLM vs Classical ML for Network Intrusion Detection under Distribution Shift and Adversarial Evasion
abstract: arXiv:2609.13511v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly benchmarked against classical machine learning for network intrusion detection (NIDS), almost always using same-dataset evaluation, and that protocol turns out to be incomplete. Evaluating XGBoost and RoBERTa-LoRA on two independently collected NetFlow v2 networks across three axes (same-dataset performance, cross-dataset transfer, and adversarial evasion) reveals no universal winner. The two models are statistically tied same-dataset. XGBoost wins decisively under cross-dataset distribution shift, by 15 points of F1 and 25 points of balanced accuracy; on the target network RoBERTa-LoRA's false positive rate reaches 0.78, leaving it barely above chance despite a superficially moderate F1. RoBERTa-LoRA wins decisively under adversarial evasion, by roughly 17 points of F1 at a representative mid-range perturbation strength, while both models hold false positive rates below 0.01 throughout. translated_title: 分布偏移与对抗逃逸下大语言模型与经典机器学习用于网络入侵检测的三轴压力测试
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型越来越多地与经典机器学习在网络入侵检测（NIDS）领域进行基准比较，但几乎总是采用同一数据集评估，而这种评估协议被证明是不完整的。在两个独立收集的 NetFlow v2 网络上，从三个维度（同数据集性能、跨数据集迁移和对抗逃逸）对 XGBoost 和 RoBERTa-LoRA 进行评估，结果显示不存在普适的赢家。两个模型在同数据集上表现统计上持平。在跨数据集分布偏移下，XGBoost 决定性地胜出，F1 领先 15 个百分点，平衡准确率领先 25 个百分点；在目标网络上，RoBERTa-LoRA 的误报率高达 0.78，尽管 F1 表面上处于中等水平，但其实际性能仅略高于随机猜测。在对抗逃逸下，RoBERTa-LoRA 则决定性地胜出，在代表性的中等扰动强度下 F1 领先约 17 个百分点，同时两个模型在整个过程中误报率均保持在 0.01 以下。
tldr: 该研究从同数据集性能、跨数据集迁移和对抗逃逸三个维度评估 XGBoost 与 RoBERTa-LoRA 用于网络入侵检测，发现两者同数据集打平，但 XGBoost 在分布偏移下显著更优，而 RoBERTa-LoRA 在对抗逃逸下显著更强，证明单一数据集评估协议是不完整的。
en_tdlr: A three-axis stress test (same-dataset, cross-dataset shift, adversarial evasion) of XGBoost vs RoBERTa-LoRA for network intrusion detection reveals no universal winner: they tie same-dataset, XGBoost decisively wins under distribution shift (+15 F1), and RoBERTa-LoRA decisively wins under adversarial evasion (+17 F1), showing same-dataset evaluation protocols are incomplete.
